Samira —

Great to connect. High level plan (short list first pass):

1) Confirm network CIDRs + routing boundary (we need your staging and prod CIDR ranges and NAT/eIP strategy).
2) VPC peering or private interconnect: pick one path (peering for simpler e2e, interconnect for heavy ingress).
3) Private endpoint configuration: secure inference endpoints (TLS + mTLS option) and allowed IP ranges.
4) On-prem appliance prep: hardware checklist, outbound egress rules, HSM/KMS connectivity plan if you plan to integrate keys.
5) Acceptance criteria & cutover steps for staging (smoke tests, latency benchmarks, and token throughput).

Immediate asks for your networking team so we can start the runbook:
- Staging CIDR and Prod CIDR
- Any required firewall egress rules for appliance (we typically need 443/9443 outbound; if you use HSM: 2222 and/or vendor-specific ports)
- Proxy / deep packet inspection in-line? (yes/no)

I've looped in Marcus (solutions engineer) for the on-prem kit details and Ben (sales) for commercial timing. Marcus — can you add the appliance pre-reqs and an install doc to the Drive link and flag anything that could push a late-feb turnup?

Thanks,

Tom / Samira —

Thanks for the details — below is a consolidated runbook and the practical recommendations based on your expected load and security posture. I've also uploaded a short install guide and an updated network diagram to the shared Drive link.

Runbook (recommended sequence):
A) Network validation (days 0–3)
  - Confirm CIDR non-overlap with Redwood staging/prod ranges (we will provide our peering subnets).
  - Exchange BGP prefixes if using interconnect; otherwise prepare IAM/VPC peering request.
  - Whitelist outbound endpoints: api.redwood.ai (443), pkg.redwood.ai (9443), metrics.redwood.ai (443) — we recommend allowing these FQDNs via DNS name whitelisting.

B) Private endpoint & mTLS (days 4–7)
  - Provision private interface endpoint in your VPC and register the FQDN we provide.
  - mTLS: exchange cert signing requests; if using internal CA we can accept signed certs or run mutual TLS via our CA.

C) On-prem appliance staging (days 8–14)
  - Hardware: x86 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, NVMe 1TB (for cache), 25Gb NIC recommended.
  - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS preferred. Ensure kernel >= 5.15.
  - Egress rules: outbound to 443 and 9443; if integrating CloudHSM, also allow outbound to HSM endpoints (we can provide hostnames).
  - Time sync and NTP, DNS resolution for private FQDNs, and optionally an HTTP proxy bypass for package pulls.
  - Airgap option: we support an offline install package (sha256-signed). If you plan to validate in a secure lab, request the airgap bundle now (takes 3 business days).

D) Acceptance & cutover (days 15–18)
  - Smoke tests: authentication, a small inference run (10–20 queries at target prompt length), latency under 120ms p50 for staging.
  - Scaling: validate KV cache warm-up and batching behavior; we will provide a synthetic load harness.

Notes on VPC peering vs interconnect:
- For 400–800 rps, VPC peering is simpler and lower ops but may complicate cross-account routing if you want central egress. If you expect burst to >1500 rps or require private bandwidth SLAs, prefer a managed interconnect.

Attachments we uploaded to Drive: redwood_onprem_pack_install_guide_v1.2.pdf (install checklist and airgap instructions), oxbridge_network_diagram.pdf (annotated).

Next steps:
- Kimberly: coordinate a 30-minute technical handoff call with your NetOps and our SRE (Marcus) this week — propose Fri 1/20 10:00 PST or Mon 1/23 09:00 PST.
- Tom: confirm whether you want the airgap bundle and whether CloudHSM keys will be provisioned ahead of staging.

If helpful, I can also drop a short list of iptables/snort rules we commonly see customers need changed in their perimeter.

Best,
Marcus Lin
